title: Taste and smell
about: Collocations for describing tastes and smells, pleasant and unpleasant: a fragrant perfume, an acquired taste, milk that has gone sour, acrid smoke, an overpowering stink, plus metaphorical ones such as develop a taste for something and smell danger.

parts.title: Negative collocations connected with smells and tastes
Over to you
parts.note: Завдання з книжки: подивитися в словнику, з якими словами вживаються taste, flavour, aroma, smell, perfume, scent і odour. Коротко: smell — найзагальніше слово, запах буває і приємний, і неприємний. Aroma, perfume і scent — приємні запахи, odour — зазвичай неприємний і трохи офіційний. Taste — смак загалом, а ще смаки людини (taste in music); flavour — особливий смак конкретної їжі чи напою (strawberry flavour).

items.pattern: the fragrant perfume of flowers / roses / blossom · fragrant flowers / herbs / soap
items.meaning: a sweet, pleasant natural smell, especially of flowers; perfume here is the smell itself, not only the liquid in a bottle
items.example: In June the whole garden is full of the **fragrant perfume** of roses.
more: On summer evenings the **fragrant perfume** of the lime trees drifts into our flat.
My grandmother keeps pots of **fragrant** herbs, like mint and basil, on her windowsill.
items.watchOut: Perfume — не лише парфуми у флаконі, а й природні пахощі квітів: the perfume of the roses. «Запашний» — fragrant /ˈfreɪɡrənt/, а не smelly: smelly означає «смердючий». Не плутай fragrant із flagrant — кричущий, явний (a flagrant breach of the rules).

items.pattern: a distinctive / rich / strong / sweet aroma (of sth) · the aroma of coffee / bread / spices
items.meaning: a pleasant smell of food or drink that is easy to recognise because it is not like any other
items.example: You can't mistake the **distinctive aroma** of cinnamon buns in that bakery.
more: Smoked paprika gives the stew a **rich aroma** and a lovely red colour.
The **sweet aroma** of baked apples filled the kitchen.
items.watchOut: Aroma /əˈrəʊmə/ — наголос на другому складі. Це трохи книжне слово про приємний запах їжі й напоїв (кави, хліба, спецій); про неприємний запах його зазвичай не вживають. «Характерний, специфічний запах» — a distinctive smell / aroma, а не a specific aroma: specific англійською — «конкретний, певний».

items.pattern: an appetising aroma / smell · appetising food / dishes · appetising (UK) / appetizing (US)
items.meaning: a smell of food that makes you feel hungry
items.example: An **appetising aroma** of fried onions was coming from the kitchen.
more: The café window was full of **appetising** cakes and pies.
After a long walk in the cold, the **appetising smell** of soup made us hurry inside.
items.watchOut: «Апетитний» — appetising, а не appetite: appetite — іменник «апетит». Tasty — смачний, коли вже куштуєш; про запах природніше appetising або delicious. Британське написання — appetising, американське — appetizing.

items.phrase: a smell wafts across / through sth
items.pattern: a smell / an aroma / a scent wafts across / through / from / in from sth · the smell of sth wafting from sth
items.meaning: a smell moves gently through the air from one place to another
items.example: The smell of grilled fish **wafted** up from the restaurant below our hotel room.
more: When I opened the window, the scent of cut grass **wafted** in from the garden.
Delicious smells were **wafting** through the house on the morning of the party.
items.watchOut: Waft /wɒft/ — про запах (а ще дим чи музику), що повільно пливе повітрям. «Запах долітав, доносився» — the smell wafted / came / drifted, а не flew: запах не «летить».

items.pattern: be an acquired taste · be a bit of an acquired taste (food, drink, music, humour)
items.meaning: something you don't like at first but start to enjoy after trying it several times
items.uk: річ на любителя; до цього треба звикнути
items.example: Blue cheese is an **acquired taste**: I hated it as a child, but I love it now.
more: Strong black tea without any sugar is an **acquired taste**.
His jokes are a bit of an **acquired taste**, but after a while you start to love them.
items.watchOut: «На любителя» — an acquired taste, з артиклем an. Не a taste for amateurs і не a lover's taste. Acquired означає «набутий»: смак, до якого звикаєш поступово.

items.pattern: a subtle flavour / taste / smell (of sth) · a subtle hint of sth
items.meaning: a delicate taste that is not strong or easy to notice
items.example: The soup has a **subtle flavour** of lemon and ginger.
more: A few drops of rose water give the dessert a **subtle flavour**.
There's a **subtle taste** of smoke in this cheese.
items.watchOut: Subtle /ˈsʌtl/ — b не вимовляється. «Тонкий смак» — a subtle або delicate flavour; a thin flavour прозвучить як «водянистий, бідний смак». Британське написання — flavour, американське — flavor.

items.pattern: a fresh / sweet / delicate scent (of sth) · the scent of pine / herbs / flowers
items.meaning: a pleasant, clean, light smell
items.example: I love the **fresh scent** of pine trees after the rain.
more: This washing powder leaves a **fresh scent** on your towels.
Each bar of soap in the shop had its own **sweet scent**: rose, honey or lavender.
items.watchOut: Scent /sent/ — c не вимовляється, звучить як sent. Scent — легкий, зазвичай приємний запах (квітів, трав, мила). Не плутай із sense — чуття, відчуття (a sense of smell).

items.pattern: bitter coffee / chocolate / medicine · a bitter taste
items.meaning: coffee with a strong, sharp taste that is not sweet and is often unpleasant
items.example: The coffee at the station café was so **bitter** that I left half of it.
more: Some children won't eat broccoli because of its slightly **bitter taste**.
My grandfather drinks his coffee black and **bitter**, without a grain of sugar.
items.watchOut: «Гіркий» про смак — bitter. Не плутай з hot / spicy (гострий, пекучий: hot chillies) і sour (кислий: sour cherries). Гірка правда, гірке розчарування — теж bitter: a bitter disappointment.

items.pattern: milk goes / turns sour · the milk has gone sour · sour milk
items.meaning: milk becomes bad and tastes and smells acid because it is too old or has been kept warm
items.example: I forgot to put the milk back in the fridge, and it **went sour**.
more: A little lemon juice will make milk **turn sour** for baking.
In my gran's village, people make cheese from **sour** milk.
items.watchOut: «Молоко скисло» — the milk has gone / turned sour або has gone off. Became sour тут звучить неприродно. Sour — кислий (лимон теж sour), а гіркий — bitter.

items.pattern: acrid smoke / smell / fumes
items.meaning: smoke with a strong, sharp smell that burns your nose and throat
items.example: Someone was burning plastic, and **acrid smoke** drifted over the gardens.
more: The **acrid smell** of burning rubber came from the car's brakes.
We closed the windows because of the **acrid smoke** from the burning fields.
items.watchOut: «Їдкий дим» — зазвичай acrid smoke. Caustic кажуть радше про хімічні речовини, що роз'їдають (caustic soda), або про уїдливі слова (a caustic remark). Вимова: /ˈækrɪd/.

items.pattern: noxious fumes / gases / chemicals · fumes from sth
items.meaning: harmful, poisonous gases or smoke, usually with a nasty smell
items.example: Keep the window open when you paint, or you'll breathe in **noxious fumes**.
more: The old factory used to pump **noxious fumes** into the air.
Never mix bleach with other cleaning products: they can give off **noxious gases**.
items.watchOut: Fumes майже завжди у множині: noxious fumes, exhaust fumes. «Випари фарби» — paint fumes, а не paint steam: steam — пара від гарячої води. Noxious /ˈnɒkʃəs/ — книжне слово «отруйний, шкідливий».

items.pattern: foul-smelling water / drains / chemicals / cheese · a foul smell
items.meaning: having a very unpleasant smell
items.example: We walked past a **foul-smelling** ditch on the way to the beach.
more: After our holiday the fridge was full of **foul-smelling** leftovers.
There's a **foul smell** coming from the bathroom drain.
items.watchOut: Foul /faʊl/ — гидкий, огидний; вимовляється так само, як fowl (птиця), і не так, як fool /fuːl/ (дурень). Перед іменником foul-smelling пишуть через дефіс: foul-smelling water.

items.pattern: body odour · BO (informal) · have body odour
items.meaning: an unpleasant smell from a person's body, caused by sweat
items.example: The bus was packed and hot, and there was a strong smell of **body odour**.
more: A good deodorant helps to stop **body odour**.
He had terrible **BO**, but nobody dared to tell him.
items.watchOut: Odour /ˈəʊdə/ — запах, зазвичай неприємний; трохи офіційне слово. Британське написання — odour, американське — odor. Розмовно кажуть BO /ˌbiː ˈəʊ/: He's got BO.

items.pattern: a strong smell / taste (of sth) · smell / taste strongly of sth
items.meaning: a smell that is very easy to notice
items.example: There's a **strong smell** of paint in the hall.
more: This garlic sauce has a really **strong taste**.
The car **smells strongly** of the dog after every trip to the beach.
items.watchOut: «Сильний запах» — a strong smell, а не a big smell. Слабкий запах — зазвичай a faint / slight smell; weak частіше кажуть про чай чи каву (weak tea).

items.pattern: have a taste (of sth) · let me have a taste · can I have a taste?
items.meaning: try a small amount of food or drink to find out what it is like
items.example: Can I **have a taste** of your ice cream? I've never tried pistachio.
more: The cheese shop lets you **have a taste** before you buy.
**Have a taste** of these strawberries. They're from our garden.
items.watchOut: «Спробуй, покуштуй» — Have a taste або Try it, а не Make a taste чи Do a taste. «Відчуваю смак» — I can taste sth, а не I feel the taste.

items.pattern: have a smell (of sth) · let me have a smell
items.meaning: smell something on purpose to find out what it is like
items.example: **Have a smell** of this candle. It's supposed to smell like the sea.
more: Let me **have a smell** of the milk before you pour it.
She picked up the melon and **had a smell** to see if it was ripe.
items.watchOut: «Понюхай» — Have a smell (of this) або Smell this, а не Make a smell. Без have значення інше: smell of sth — пахнути чимось (Your coat smells of smoke).

items.pattern: sth smells / tastes off · sth is off · sth has gone off
items.meaning: seems no longer fresh or good to eat because it is too old
items.example: Don't eat that chicken. It **smells off**.
more: This yoghurt **tastes** a bit **off**. Check the date on the pot.
The fish had **gone off** by the time we got home from the beach.
items.watchOut: У британській англійській про зіпсовану їжу кажуть smells off / is off / has gone off. Spoiled (has spoiled) у цьому значенні звучить більш по-американськи. Не плутай з The lights are off — світло вимкнене.

items.pattern: an overpowering stink / smell (of sth) · sth stinks (of sth) · stink – stank – stunk
items.meaning: a very strong, unpleasant smell that is hard to bear
items.example: When we opened the cupboard under the sink, there was an **overpowering stink** of damp.
more: Someone had left wet trainers in the car, and the **stink** was **overpowering**.
Her new perfume was a bit **overpowering** in the small lift.
items.watchOut: Stink /stɪŋk/ — сморід, розмовне слово; stench /stentʃ/ — ще сильніше й книжніше. Overpowering — такий сильний, що аж збиває з ніг; так кажуть і про приємний запах, якого забагато (an overpowering perfume). Дієслово неправильне: stink – stank – stunk.

items.pattern: give off a smell / fumes / smoke / heat · give off – gave off – given off
items.meaning: produce a smell (or smoke, heat) that goes out into the air
items.example: The old cheese at the back of the fridge was **giving off** a terrible smell.
more: Lilies **give off** such a strong smell that I never put them in the bedroom.
This heater **gives off** a funny smell when you first turn it on.
items.watchOut: «Виділяти запах» — give off a smell, з off; просто give a smell не кажуть. Так само give off smoke / fumes / heat. Give away — віддати або видати таємницю, це про інше.

items.pattern: a revolting / terrible / awful stench (of sth)
items.meaning: an extremely unpleasant, disgusting smell; stench is even stronger than stink
items.example: A **revolting stench** came out of the lunch box he'd forgotten in his school bag.
more: The **stench** from the fish market was **revolting** in the midday heat.
Nobody would sit near the bins in the park because of the **revolting stench**.
items.watchOut: Revolting тут не про бунт (revolt — повстання), а «огидний, аж нудить» = disgusting. Stench /stentʃ/ — сильніше й книжніше слово, ніж stink.

items.pattern: a whiff of sth (perfume, smoke, garlic) · catch / get / detect a whiff of sth
items.meaning: a slight smell that you notice for a moment
items.uk: легкий запах (парфумів), ледь відчутний дух чогось
items.example: As she walked past, I caught a **whiff of perfume**.
more: I got a **whiff** of garlic when he leant over to talk to me.
There was a **whiff** of smoke in the air: someone nearby was having a barbecue.
items.watchOut: Whiff /wɪf/ — короткий легкий запах, що його відчуваєш на мить. «Відчути запах» — catch / get a whiff of sth або I can smell sth, а не feel a smell: feel про запах не кажуть.

items.phrase: leave a bad / unpleasant taste in your mouth
items.pattern: sth leaves a bad / unpleasant / nasty taste in your mouth
items.meaning: makes you feel unhappy or uncomfortable for some time afterwards
items.example: The way the shop assistant spoke to my mum **left a bad taste in my mouth**.
more: We won, but the arguing after the match **left an unpleasant taste in everyone's mouth**.
Their rude email **left a nasty taste in my mouth**, so I never used that company again.
items.watchOut: «Залишити неприємний осад» — leave a bad / unpleasant taste in your mouth. Sediment — осад лише в рідині (на дні пляшки), метафорично так не кажуть. Дієслово — leave (left), а не stay чи keep.

items.pattern: taste freedom / success / victory · get a taste of freedom
items.meaning: experience something good, such as freedom or success, often for the first time
items.example: After years of strict rules at home, she **tasted freedom** for the first time at university.
more: Once the team had **tasted success**, they wanted to win every match.
That first summer job gave me a **taste of freedom**: my own money at last.
items.watchOut: «Відчути смак свободи» — taste freedom; feel the taste of freedom — калька. Так само taste success, taste victory.

items.phrase: share the same taste in sth
items.pattern: share / have the same taste in music / films / clothes · have good taste in sth
items.meaning: like the same kinds of things as another person
items.example: My sister and I **share the same taste in** films, so choosing what to watch is easy.
more: We don't **share the same taste in** clothes at all: he likes bright colours, I prefer grey.
Twins don't always **share the same taste in** food.
items.watchOut: Смаки людини — taste in sth (з in): taste in music, taste in clothes. Taste of sth — смак їжі: the taste of honey. «У нас однакові смаки» — We share / have the same taste.

items.pattern: develop / acquire a taste for sth / for doing sth · have a taste for sth
items.meaning: slowly start to like something and want more of it
items.uk: увійти у смак, поступово полюбити щось
items.example: Since our trip to Lisbon, my dad has **developed a taste for** seafood.
more: My daughter has **developed a taste for** old black-and-white films.
Living by the sea, he **developed a taste for** early-morning swims.
items.watchOut: Develop a taste for sth — з for, не to і не of. Порівняй: taste in sth — смаки людини (taste in music), a taste for sth — потяг, любов до чогось (a taste for spicy food).

items.pattern: smell danger / trouble · smell a rat (= feel that something is wrong or dishonest)
items.meaning: sense that something dangerous or bad is going to happen
items.example: The cat **smelt danger** and hid under the bed as soon as the vet's bag came out.
more: My grandad could always **smell trouble** before it started.
The kids were far too quiet, and I **smelt a rat**: they'd found the biscuits.
items.watchOut: Минулий час — smelt (британське) або smelled. Smell a rat — запідозрити щось недобре, а не буквально «почути запах щура». «Відчувати небезпеку» — smell / sense danger.

items.pattern: get the flavour of sth (a place, a book, a talk) · give sb a flavour of sth
items.meaning: understand the general idea or character of something without knowing every detail
items.uk: вловити суть, відчути загальний дух (настрій) чогось
items.example: After two days in Rome, we'd only **got the flavour of** the city, but we loved it.
more: Just reading the menu gave us a **flavour of** the local cooking.
This short video will **give you a flavour of** what the course is like.
items.watchOut: «Вловити суть» — get the flavour of sth або get the gist of sth. Flavour тут не про смак, а про загальний характер чогось. Catch the flavour кажуть рідко, природніше get.

warmup.q: These pickled cucumbers are an ___ taste.
warmup.explain: «На любителя» — an acquired taste: до цього смаку треба звикнути.

warmup.uk: У цього чаю тонкий жасминовий смак.
warmup.q: This tea has a ___ flavour of jasmine.
warmup.explain: Тонкий, ледь відчутний смак — a subtle flavour. Thin — тонкий за товщиною, а про смак означає «водянистий».
Скисло — has gone sour (або has gone off). Bitter — гіркий.

warmup.q: Can I ___ a taste of your soup?

warmup.explain: Про зіпсовану їжу кажуть smells off / is off / has gone off.

warmup.uk: Я вловила легкий запах кави із сусідньої квартири.
warmup.q: I caught a ___ of coffee from the flat next door.
warmup.explain: Catch a whiff of sth — вловити легкий запах. Feel про запах не кажуть.

warmup.q: The conversation left a bad ___ in my mouth.
warmup.explain: Неприємний осад — a bad taste in your mouth. Sediment — осад лише в рідині.

warmup.uk: Ми з чоловіком маємо однакові смаки в книжках.
warmup.q: My husband and I share the same taste ___ books.
warmup.explain: Смаки людини — taste in sth: taste in music, taste in clothes.

A.q: Spicy Korean food was an ___ taste for my parents, but now they cook it every week.
A.explain: An acquired taste — те, що подобається не одразу, а згодом, коли звикнеш.

A.q: As we walked along the beach, the smell of grilled corn ___ towards us from a little stall.
A.explain: Waft — про запах, що повільно пливе повітрям. Запах не «летить» (fly).

A.q: Driving through Provence, we opened the windows to enjoy the ___ perfume of the lavender fields.
A.explain: Fragrant — запашний, приємний. Smelly — смердючий, noxious — отруйний.

B.q: The council closed the swimming pool after a chemical leak released ___ fumes.
Cotton clothes are better than nylon in summer because they help prevent body ___.
B.explain: Body odour — неприємний запах поту. Aroma і perfume — приємні запахи.

B.q: This grapefruit juice is too ___ for me; I'll add some honey.
B.explain: Bitter — гіркий. Acrid — їдкий, так кажуть про дим і запах.

C.q: Have a ___ of this shampoo. Isn't it lovely?
C.explain: Have a smell (of sth) — понюхати. Scent — сам запах, а не дія; stink — сморід.

C.q: The drains outside the restaurant were giving ___ a terrible smell.
C.explain: Give off a smell — виділяти запах.

C.q: When we lifted the lid of the compost bin, a ___ stench hit us.
C.explain: Revolting stench — огидний сморід. Fragrant — запашний, subtle — ледь відчутний.

D.q: My nephew has started to ___ a taste for classical music.
D.explain: Develop a taste for sth — поступово полюбити щось.

D.q: My mum can always ___ danger: she called me just as I was about to do something stupid.
Her unkind comments at the wedding left a bad ___ in my mouth.
D.explain: Leave a bad taste in your mouth — залишити неприємний осад.

example.title: A morning at the market
example.uk:
У суботу ми пішли на старий ринок у центрі міста. Біля входу нас зустріли запашні пахощі квітів, а з пекарні неподалік линув запах свіжого хліба. Мій чоловік покуштував трохи козячого сиру. «Це на любителя», — сказав він і скривився.

Потім ми проходили повз рибні ряди. Я вловила легкий запах чогось явно несвіжого, а біля смітників стояв нестерпний сморід. Ми поспішили до маленької кав'ярні, де характерний аромат кави з кардамоном змусив нас одразу сісти.

У їжі смаки в нас збігаються не завжди, але ця кава сподобалася нам обом. Ми ще говорили про її тонкий смак, коли повернулися додому.
example.en:
On Saturday we went to the old market in the town centre. The [[fragrant perfume|a1]] of flowers greeted us at the entrance, and the smell of fresh bread [[wafted|a4]] from a bakery nearby. My husband [[had a taste|c2]] of some goat's cheese. 'It's [[an acquired taste|a5]],' he said, pulling a face.

Then we passed the fish stalls. I caught a [[whiff|c8]] of something that definitely [[smelt off|c4]], and near the bins there was an [[overpowering stink|c5]]. We hurried on to a little café, where the [[distinctive aroma|a2]] of cardamom coffee made us sit down at once.

We don't always [[share the same taste in|d3]] food, but we both loved that coffee. We were still talking about its [[subtle flavour|a6]] when we got home.
